title: Saladin Takes Jerusalem Without a Massacre
text:
In July 1187 the Muslim ruler Saladin destroyed the army of the crusader Kingdom of Jerusalem at the Battle of Hattin. In September he besieged Jerusalem itself. The city was crowded with refugees and had few knights. Its defense was led by Balian of Ibelin, a nobleman who had escaped from Hattin.

When the walls were breached, Balian went to negotiate. According to the Arab chronicler Ibn al-Athir, he warned Saladin that if no terms were given, the defenders would kill their Muslim prisoners, destroy the Dome of the Rock and the holy places, kill their own families, and fight to the death. Saladin, who had earlier sworn to take the city by the sword as the crusaders had done in 1099, agreed to terms.

The inhabitants could leave in safety after paying a ransom: ten dinars for a man, five for a woman, two for a child. Saladin entered the city on October 2, 1187. There was no massacre. According to chroniclers on both sides, Saladin and his brother al-Adil released thousands of poor people without ransom.

Many who could not pay were still enslaved. But the contrast with the bloodshed of 1099 made Saladin's name respected even in Christian Europe.
lesson: How you behave at the moment of victory shapes your reputation long after. Restraint can win the respect even of those you defeated.
source: Imad ad-Din al-Isfahani; Ibn al-Athir, The Complete History; Old French Continuation of William of Tyre (Ernoul)
caveat: The numbers freed without ransom, and enslaved, differ greatly between the Muslim and Christian chroniclers.
